chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In the Siwak (brushing the teeth) are twelve qualities: It is from the Sunnah, and a cleansing for the mouth, and a polishing for the vision, and it pleases the Lord, and it removes the phlegm, and it increases in memorization, and it whitens the teeth, and it multiplies the good deeds, and it removes the cavities, and it strengthens the gums, and it makes the food desirable, and the Angels are happy with it.
ai.seo_question: What are the twelve benefits of using Siwak according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines twelve specific virtues of the Siwak, blending physical hygiene with spiritual purification. It emphasizes the practice as a Sunnah that not only pleases God and brings angelic joy but also enhances physical health by strengthening gums and improving vision, reflecting the holistic approach to well-being in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Ibn Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘In brushing of the teeth are twelve qualities – It is from the Sunnah, and a cleansing for the mouth, and a polishing for the vision, and a Pleasure of the Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and it removes the phlegm, and increases in the memorisation, and it whitens the teeth, and it amplifies the Rewards, and removes the cavities, and strengthens the gums, and it makes one desirous of the food, and the Angels are happy with it’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Ubayd al-Dihqan from Durust from ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

In tooth brushing there are twelve qualities. It is an act of Sunnah, it cleanses the mouth, sharpens eyesight, earns Allah’s pleasure, dispels phlegm, improves memory, whitens the teeth, amplifies the list of good deeds, banishes cavities, strengthens gums, increases appetite for food and it makes the angels happy.’”
